_comment: The map base: a hole in hell's ground, one ring deck round the void the tower stands in, with a lava river cut into it. Authored in WORLD coordinates -- instance at identity: deck at y=23.0 (r 46.7..57.3) under a rock ceiling at y=31.5 (the gallery is a cutout, open toward the void), lava sea at y=-11.05, rim at y=330. The river is NOT a sheet laid on anything: between bearings 292.3 and 338.3 the deck's own surface is dropped 0.3 m to y=22.7 between two sloped banks, and those faces take the LavaRiver material. The channel carries on into both walls the same way -- cut 0.4 m back into the shaft wall from 293 to 338 deg, y 22.7 up to 30.7, and 0.4 m back into the pit wall all the way down to the sea -- so the lava is always map_base's own faces, defined by banks, never an overlay. Seven platforms with flat square 2.4 x 2.4 m tops at y=23.0 stand 0.3 m out of it; three fins rise off the inner ones. Prison cells (arched glowing recesses with carved columns) are carved into the pit faces, visual only, and none in the channel. SIX surfaces: the hell rock as one tiling sheet per class through lib/texel.py (rock, shade, ember; world-projected at 0.05 m per texel, no atlas windows), the atlas kept only for the S3 cracks' glowing cell (their UVs exactly as before), LavaRiver on a tiling sheet streaked along the flow, and LavaSea on the pit floor: Ryan's own 256 px tile (maps/bentham_ring/textures/lava_albedo.png) repeated every 5 m in world x,y, its emissive derived from the albedo so the orange glows and the crust stays dark. All single-sided. Five lip walls stand on the pit lip (r 46.9..48.2, foot buried at y 22.2): the screen across the start (-8..14 deg, head 4.6 m over the deck) and one at each section boundary (61.7..71.3, 134.2..143.8, 199.2..208.8, 281.2..290.8; ~8 m long, 3 m tall, ragged domed head), tangential to the ring, no mouth, nothing across the deck -- the runner passes each on the outer side and it hides a standing body on the lane from the guard's eye. MapBaseCollision is the purpose-built collider shipped as a `-colonly` node (deck minus the channel, a flat surface at the lava height minus the platform footprints, the platform tops and sides, the fins, pit wall, courtyard disc, outer wall, flat ceiling); Godot turns it into a StaticBody3D + ConcavePolygonShape3D and drops its mesh, so `surfaces` counts only what is drawn. S3, the demon pad grid, is bearings 143..202 of the deck re-laid on its own grid from one layout (the S3 block of tools/modelling/maps/bentham_ring/map_base_build.py): a FLAT deck at lane height tiled with demon_pad scene nodes in rows and columns, one path carved through the grid by the cells left pad-free, three pads left in the path to be jumped, and one continuous ragged rock wall of the deck's own rock (crest about 2.5..3.0 m, rising from the lip on a 0.88 m footprint with a near-vertical face to the deck) along the path's pit side, tall enough to hide a standing body on the path from the guard and low enough that every crack launch's apex is seen. No lava and no TrapVolume in it.
